record.paper_title: 25 Open Questions About Vector Bundles and Their Moduli
record.original_question: Let X be a complex projective manifold of dimension greater than one. Instead of a single Higgs field E → E ⊗ Ω_X^1 or a single coHiggs field E → E ⊗ T_X, consider r ≥ 2 such fields on the same vector bundle E, with an appropriate integrability condition such as f_i ∧ f_j = 0 for all i,j. What is the optimal extension of the notions of Higgs bundle and coHiggs bundle to this multi-field setting?

evidence.quote: Question 9. What are the optimal extensions of the concepts of Higgs and coHiggs bundles to include r fields in place of 1 in the case of manifolds of dimension greater than one?
We prefer the strongest one: impose that fi ∧ fj = 0 for all i, j.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex projective manifold with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} X > 1$, and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on $X$. Recall that a Higgs field on $E$ is a holomorphic morphism $f \colon E \to E \otimes \Omega_X^1$ satisfying $f \wedge f = 0$, and a coHiggs field on $E$ is a holomorphic morphism $f \colon E \to E \otimes T_X$ satisfying $f \wedge f = 0$.

Fix an integer $r \geq 2$. Consider $r$-tuples of morphisms $(f_1, \dots, f_r)$ on the same bundle $E$, where each $f_i$ is either of "Higgs type" $E \to E \otimes \Omega_X^1$ or of "coHiggs type" $E \to E \otimes T_X$, subject to the strong integrability condition
$$f_i \wedge f_j = 0 \quad \text{for all } i, j \in \{1, \dots, r\}.$$

Determine the optimal extension of the notions of Higgs bundle and coHiggs bundle to this multi-field setting on higher-dimensional manifolds: namely, formulate the appropriate definitions (including suitable notions of (semi)stability), establish the existence and basic properties of moduli spaces of such objects, and identify the integrability/compatibility conditions that yield the most natural and well-behaved theory generalizing the classical $r=1$ case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open foundational question about the proper definition of multi-field Higgs/coHiggs bundles on higher-dimensional manifolds. Web search reveals related work on co-Higgs bundles and 2-nilpotent coHiggs structures, but no comprehensive proposal addressing the optimal extension to r ≥ 2 fields with the strong integrability condition f_i ∧ f_j = 0 in dimensions greater than one. No definitive resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of co-Higgs bundles (Rayan thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational treatment of co-Higgs bundles with single field; multi-field higher-dimensional extension not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: The standard theory of co-Higgs bundles in the literature treats the single-field case; multi-field extensions in higher dimensions remain to be developed.

status_evidence.title: Co-Higgs bundles on P^1
status_evidence.snippet: Studies co-Higgs bundles in the one-dimensional setting where integrability is automatic.
status_evidence.claim: Existing co-Higgs bundle results focus on dim X = 1, where the integrability condition is automatic.

status_evidence.title: Higgs bundle (nLab)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard definition uses a single Higgs field with f ∧ f = 0.
status_evidence.claim: The classical definition is for a single Higgs field; the multi-field optimal generalization is not part of the standard theory.
